title: Support symlinks in interrupted-merge worktree archives
body:
## What

Support Git mode `120000` (symbolic links) in structured interrupted-merge archives, without introducing another archive mode, database, or worktree-specific exception.

## Evidence and scope

A read-only capture attempt on a retained merge worktree reaches `merge:unsupported_head_entry` because HEAD contains tracked symlinks. `merge_working_paths` currently permits only `100644` and `100755`; the merge working-file path also explicitly refuses symlinks. The ordinary preservation path already handles symlink metadata. No production worktree should be modified or removed while implementing this fix.

The separate local FETCH_HEAD preservation change is not part of this issue. Keep it separate. Tests for this issue can use merges without FETCH_HEAD.

## Reproducer

In the existing disposable lifecycle fixture, commit a tracked symlink pointing to `mixed.txt`, then use `start_conflicted_merge()` to create a conflict in that regular file. Invoke the fixture's `archive()` helper. The baseline refuses the symlink mode in the index or HEAD (`merge:unsupported_index_entry` or `merge:unsupported_head_entry`) instead of preserving the otherwise supported merge. Expected: preserve the link target as bytes without reading the destination, restore the same index stages, and allow normal merge resolution. A read-only production capture independently reproduced `merge:unsupported_head_entry`; no source data was altered.

## Implementation targets and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_merge_capture.py`: permit symlink tree entries and capture link targets without following them.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_merge_index.py`: validate/reconstruct mode `120000` for staged and conflicted entries; inspect the existing working-state representation before extending it.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_merge_restore.py`: restore symlinks while retaining no-follow parent traversal and safe file/link replacement.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_merge_objects.py`: reuse existing blob/object-closure verification, rather than introducing a parallel object importer.
- Reference `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_filesystem.py` and the existing normal archive/tar preservation helpers for link metadata and descriptor-relative filesystem access. Reuse existing primitives where appropriate.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_archive_merge_cases.py` through the existing `test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` harness. Update `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regular files, symlinks and absent entries share the existing merge preservation flow. Link destinations may be missing or outside the worktree: preserve the link itself, never read/copy its destination.
2. Capture and restore retain exact link-target bytes, Git index modes/stages, resolve-undo and current working state.
3. No writes through symlink parents; malicious or raced parent replacement must fail closed. Do not enable submodules or directory/file conflict support incidentally.
4. Existing archives without symlinks remain readable. Any representation extension must validate explicitly and fail closed in unsupported readers.
5. Preserve ignored-file exclusion and source-change detection. No forced production GC, merge abort, source deletion, or relaxed integrity checks.

## Verification

Use disposable repositories in the existing archive lifecycle harness: ordinary/dangling links, changed target, staged and conflicted symlink entries, regular-file/link transitions, preservation after source loss and GC, merge continuation/abort, and parent-symlink escape rejection with an untouched outside sentinel. Run scoped Ruff/Bandit and existing merge round-trip regressions. Validate the real retained worktree only read-only until separate operational authority and verified preservation apply.

## Ownership and planning

The operator explicitly requested a separate issue and immediate interactive claim; this session owns implementation, not a background worker.

Pre-flight: memory recalled; target-file history and related open PRs checked; no matching open merge-symlink issue found. Related archive-metadata PR #36344 must not be overwritten. Tier: standard, using the decided existing Git/tar preservation model with focused safety verification. Draft PR not seeded before implementation. Rollback: revert the isolated implementation commit; existing archives and production source worktrees remain untouched.

title: Unify lifecycle filesystem validation diagnostics and shared Python primitives
body:
## Goal

Unify lifecycle filesystem-validation diagnostics and genuinely shared Python primitives without changing permission policies or broadening the archive producer's responsibilities. Follow-up to merged PR #36364, which fixed owned 0755 archive roots without chmod.

## Evidence

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/storage.py:45-49` implements `_private()` inside SQLite storage, but cleanup, retirement, upgrade and legacy modules import it for non-database objects. Its single error cannot distinguish object type, owner or permission failures.
- `worker_lifecycle/archive_path.py` has a separate descriptor-relative chain validator with distinct root/intermediate/private-leaf policies. Those differences are intentional and must not be erased by consolidation.
- `worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py:106-115` accepts only restricted stable ValueError strings as reasons; current archive errors containing paths fall back to `ValueError`.
- `worker_lifecycle/registry.py:220-231` likewise reduces most ValueError instances to the class name. Improving exception text alone therefore does not ensure actionable CLI diagnostics.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh:495-496` creates archive parents normally and each new archive with 0700. Existing root permissions are not changed. This producer behavior is not the reported defect.

## Recommended implementation boundary

1. Separate filesystem validation from SQLite storage ownership. Extract only reusable metadata validation/error primitives into a small dependency-free Python module within `worker_lifecycle`; choose the exact module name during implementation. Do not introduce a universal permission engine, plugin registry or boolean-heavy API.
2. Keep explicit validators for private state files/directories and archive path chains. Preserve the current permission policies, descriptor-relative no-follow traversal, sticky-ancestor exception and trust assumptions. Retain a compatibility adapter for `_private` if needed to keep consumer migration small.
3. Introduce a typed validation error with stable reason codes and allowlisted context (role, offending component, relevant mode/errno). Preserve existing exit/status semantics and deliberately map legacy codes where callers rely on them. Audit affected callers before changing public JSON fields.
4. Serialize these typed errors consistently in registry CLI, cleanup item reports and legacy CLI. Do not weaken sanitization for arbitrary exceptions, subprocess argv/stdout/stderr or database contents. Keep detailed paths within intended local/operator diagnostics; do not automatically publish them to public issue/PR content or telemetry.
5. Use Python standard-library calls and in-process imports. Do not add shell wrappers, subprocess-based stat/chmod probes, dependencies or repeated interpreter launches. Do not change archive creation policy or rewrite the shell archive orchestration in this task.

## Policy invariants

- Existing permissions are never silently changed; no chmod/chown migration.
- Owned non-externally-writable archive roots/intermediate directories may remain 0755; archive leaves remain private.
- Registry initialization continues creating new private state directories and files, with existing private-state checks preserved.
- Unsafe preservation paths must not authorize source deletion; dry-run remains non-mutating.
- Same-UID/admin and extended ACL limitations are preserved and documented, not silently claimed solved. ACL support or policy changes require a separate design decision.

## Files and reference patterns

Primary files: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/storage.py`, `archive_path.py`, `cleanup.py`, `registry.py`, `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker-legacy-cleanup.py`, and `worker_lifecycle/bundle.py`. Inventory `_private` importers before deciding whether small import updates are necessary. Reference the existing `ObservationUnavailable`/`StoreConflict` handling for typed errors without inheriting unrelated behavior. Update `CLEANUP.md`, `REGISTRY.md` or `LEGACY-CLEANUP.md` only where their contract changes.

## Acceptance and verification

- CLI and per-item reports retain a stable actionable filesystem reason instead of a bare `ValueError`, with intentionally controlled context.
- One shared error/metadata mechanism is reused where appropriate; archive traversal and private-state policies remain explicit, not flattened into one permission requirement.
- Existing 0755 archive regressions, private-state rejection, wrong-owner/type/symlink/external-write rejection, no-chmod and dry-run guarantees still pass.
- Exercise actual registry/legacy CLI JSON and cleanup reports using disposable fixtures; cover sanitization and exception translation with existing unittest infrastructure.
- New Python modules are included in the registry validator bundle; isolated bundle import passes.
- Run focused Ruff, package mypy, the repository annotation-compatibility checker, relevant existing storage/archive/cleanup tests and configured quality gates. Validate Linux/macOS support through available tooling; distinguish untested platforms from verified results.
- No new shell scripts or test framework. No speedup claim without a before/after measurement; this task should avoid adding subprocesses to the validation path.

## Out of scope

Archive-format changes, a wholesale shell-to-Python rewrite, SQLite schema changes, relaxing private-state policy, automatic permission repair, new ACL enforcement, or unrelated lifecycle behavior changes.

title: aidevops update skips same-version worker-lifecycle-only deployments
body:
## Problem

Same-version update reconciliation can leave deployed worker-lifecycle code behind the fetched source. `_update_already_current` in `aidevops.sh` filters the deployed-to-source diff through a fixed path set that excludes `.agents/worker-lifecycle/`.

## Observed evidence

- After a maintainer reported completing the normal update, the clean source checkout was at `2abbe8a37fdf284218374d6a3e3dda8567d687b8` (PR #36363), while the deployed SHA stamp remained `2a8e11f19d578cf74598702dc6211ff87c8cd1cc`.
- The diff between those commits consists of eight files exclusively under `.agents/worker-lifecycle/`. Both report version 3.39.108.
- The installed registry CLI still lacked the `upgrade` command and the existing schema-1 store still lacked admission support. Worktree creation had refused with `OperationalError`, consistent with issue #36358.
- Inspection of `_update_already_current` confirms that this module-only diff cannot trigger its same-version redeployment branch. The original terminal update output was not captured, so this is not an attribution of every earlier update phase.
- Explicit maintainer-approved `setup.sh --non-interactive --stage agents` deployed the fix. The installed CLI then exposed `upgrade`, registry status reported schema 2, and supported native worktree creation succeeded without disabling lifecycle or manually modifying the registry.

## Implementation scope

- Update `aidevops.sh` same-version deployed-SHA reconciliation so runtime module changes under `.agents/worker-lifecycle/` trigger the normal serialized deployment transaction.
- Check corresponding drift filters in `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` and `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper-check.sh` for the same missing runtime directory; change only affected filters.
- Use existing patterns in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cmd-update-sha-drift.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`. Keep setup's supported atomic deployment/verification and rollback behavior rather than copying individual modules.

### Files Scope

- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`

title: Block raw agent git worktree add to require controlled-creation receipts
body:
## Problem

Agent-issued raw `git worktree add` bypasses controlled creation. Subsequent admission can enroll the worktree without a `created-worktree` receipt. This bypasses normal receipt-backed retirement and makes cleanup dependent on explicit recovery evidence.

## Why it matters

This is a controlled-creation provenance gap, not a demonstrated permanent disk leak. A raw-created worktree can subsequently enter the registry through admission of registered runs and, once the recovery prerequisites are satisfied, be retired through the recovery path.

Recovery succeeded in the observed case, with this event chain: `close-admission` → `worktree-recovery-authorized` → `wip-preserved` → `retirement-planned` → `worktree-retired`. A missing creation receipt alone did not prevent preservation and retirement. Active or uncertain owners still prevent retirement; admission is not permission to delete a live worktree.

The case where no registered process ever works in the raw-created tree has not been tested. Its cleanup outcome remains unverified; this issue does not claim a confirmed permanent leak for that case. The fix ensures controlled-creation receipts from the outset rather than relying on later recovery evidence.

## Reproducer

Examples use placeholder paths and names:

```bash
git worktree add -b feature/example /path/to/worktrees/example origin/main
git -C /path/to/repository worktree add /path/to/worktrees/example
```

## Verified evidence

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/worker-write-fence.mjs:20` includes `add` among mutating worktree subcommands. Lines 119–130 check the Git target against worker roots, not controlled creation.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-side-effect-classifier.mjs:9` classifies direct `git worktree add`; its pattern does not cover intervening Git global options such as `-C`. Classification does not prohibit creation.
- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py:344` delegates Bash command policy. Policy-only checks of both example forms returned `allow`, rule `command.default-allow`; no worktrees were created.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md:435–438` permits explicit recovery-evidence cleanup without a creation receipt when all bound owners are admitted and ended. Therefore, claiming these trees can never be retired would be too strong. Enrollment alone remains insufficient.

## Expected behaviour

Reject direct agent calls to `git worktree add` in both OpenCode and the Claude hook, with guidance to use `worktree-helper.sh add` or `aidevops worktree add`. Preserve helper-managed creation, its internal Git invocation, and controlled-creation receipts.

## Implementation guidance

Prefer the shared parsed command policy consumed by both runtimes over inconsistent regex-only guards. Trace the OpenCode integration before editing; do not limit enforcement to the headless-only write fence. Handle supported shell wrappers and Git global options using existing parser patterns. Do not add an agent-settable raw-creation bypass.

### Files to inspect / modify

- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_git_matchers.py`
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_config.py`
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_evaluation.py`
- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/worker-write-fence.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-side-effect-classifier.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`
- `tests/test-git-safety-guard.py`

Exact policy configuration and OpenCode integration files must be resolved during implementation. Do not change retirement authority or fabricate creation receipts for existing trees.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both runtimes reject raw creation, including `git -C … worktree add`, and explain the helper route.
- Interactive and worker calls receive the same creation requirement.
- Helper-mediated creation succeeds and records controlled-creation provenance.
- Read-only worktree commands remain allowed; unrelated safety rules remain intact.
- Existing focused policy and runtime-hook tests cover rejected raw forms and allowed helper forms.

## Verification

Run policy-only checks using `python3 .agents/scripts/command-policy-helper.py check-command --command '<example>'`; both raw forms must change from allow to forbid. Run existing command-policy shell tests, Python hook tests, and OpenCode git-safety-gate tests using their documented entrypoints. Exercise helper creation in an isolated disposable repository and verify the receipt without weakening cleanup safeguards.

## Ownership

Claimed by the current interactive session; do not dispatch parallel work while that claim is active. Implementation and verification are tracked in PR #36383.

- `setup.sh`, `aidevops.sh` (call rollback on convergence failure)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh` (distinct candidate SHA)

Ownership guard at `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh:1573-1586`: only roll back if the active bundle is still the candidate, so a concurrent successful deployment is not undone.

title: fix(lifecycle): retain interactive ownership after bounded worktree creation
body:
## Observed defect

An interactive worktree for PR #36387 was archived and retired by scheduled cleanup while the parent OpenCode session was still completing that PR. Its commits were already pushed and the preservation journal confirms an archive, so no work loss is claimed. Nevertheless, an active interactive writer must not become eligible merely because its creation command ends.

## Reproducer

The worktree was created through the managed `worktree-helper.sh add <branch>` path inside the bounded-operation tool. Subsequent edits, checks, commits and pushes were issued by the same interactive session. At the next CI-wait invocation, the worktree path no longer existed. Read-only registry inspection found:

- 2026-11-01 17:54:51 UTC: creation admission/binding and `created-worktree`.
- 18:25:23: `close-admission`.
- 18:25:25: `wip-preserved`, then `retirement-planned`.
- 18:25:26: `retirement-removing`, then `worktree-retired`.

The pushed head remained `8496b58c50564ec0b14a4468c40146b377f43882`. PR #36387 was subsequently merged using remote evidence. Private archive and registry identifiers are deliberately omitted.

## Scope

Trace which native process identity is admitted at creation and whether subsequent interactive tool writes admit the actual session owner. Do not assume the producer, bounded-operation supervisor, or an arbitrary ancestor PID is the session owner. Fix the observed ownership propagation/coverage gap rather than disabling cleanup, adding grace-period heuristics, or fabricating creation events.

Start at these existing paths (exact root cause is not yet established):

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/creation.py`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-runtime.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/pre-edit-check-tool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/pre-edit-check-process.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/runtime-owner.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-worktree-ownership.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs`

### Integration evidence (GH#36392)

The bounded supervisor replaces `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID` with its own PID and the session with the operation ID before spawning the creation command. The manager knows the authenticated session, while pre-edit resolves runtime ownership using matching session and process-start proof. Extract that resolver for reuse, propagate its owner through bounded spawning, retain independent supervisor admission for existing targets, and admit successful pre-edit checks into the native registry. Existing mutation/Bash admission must use the same resolver. These adjacent paths are necessary for the authorized outcome; cleanup, archive, and worker-launch policy remain unchanged. Collision discovery found no competing open PR or claim. Verification: existing bounded/pre-edit suites, disposable native-registry worktree regression, lifecycle unittest discovery, and configured scoped Ruff/mypy for Linux and Darwin where available.

### Reference patterns

Use the existing bounded-operation and pre-edit tests under `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/` and lifecycle tests under `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/`; extend the scope after identifying the exact regression case.

Related changes #36377/#36382 enforce controlled creation and missing-runtime coverage behavior; verify whether this path bypasses or inadequately satisfies those contracts. Open issue search for worktree owner/bounded found no specific duplicate; #35359 is the broader rollout umbrella.

## Acceptance and verification

1. Reproduce with disposable worktrees: create via a bounded operation, let that command exit, continue an identified interactive session against the worktree, and run cleanup.
2. While the actual session owner remains active, cleanup must retain the worktree. Ownerless/unknown identity must not silently become complete coverage.
3. Demonstrate legitimate cleanup once all admitted owners really end, and unchanged safety for existing worker launches.
4. Use the existing test suites and scoped Ruff/mypy (both configured Linux and Darwin platforms) plus relevant OpenCode plugin checks. No production deletion is required for verification.

High-priority safety follow-up. Worker-ready implementation: investigate the evidenced path, fix it, and submit a separately scoped PR; do not modify unrelated worktrees or weaken archive verification.

title: Make test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh hermetic on hosts with real Homebrew tools
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh` fails on `main` (`bd39863`) on a macOS host with real Homebrew tools installed. The test exits 1 at line 62-63, where `tool-version-check.sh --category brew --update --quiet` returns non-zero, before any of its assertions run. Nothing is printed: stdout goes to `/dev/null`, and `bash -x` shows only the call and the trap cleanup.

## Reproducer

On macOS with Homebrew `glab`, `rg`, `shellcheck` and `jq` installed, at `main` `bd39863`:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh   # exit 1, no output
bash -x .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh  # last step: tool-version-check.sh --category brew --update --quiet, then trap cleanup
```

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh`

## Likely cause (unverified)

The test stubs only `gh`, `jq`, `brew` and `sudo`, and keeps the host `PATH` after its stub directory (`SYSTEM_PATH`). So every other `BREW_TOOLS` entry (`glab`, `wt`, `rg`, `shellcheck`, plus the Homebrew-owned OpenCode/Claude Code specs from `_oc_brew_tool_spec` / `_cc_brew_tool_spec`) resolves to the real host binary. The stub `brew` reports `stable=1.0.0` for those, and `brew list --formula` is false for anything but `gh`. The run then ends with an update failure or unverified result, and the summary exits non-zero. The sibling test `test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh` avoids this by stubbing every CLI in the category (see its `for cli in ...` lists).

## How

1. Reproduce: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh`, then drop `>/dev/null` at line 63 to see the summary. Confirm which tool is responsible.
2. Make the test hermetic: stub every `BREW_TOOLS` command at a current version (pattern: `test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh` around line 110), or restrict PATH to the stub dir plus the minimal system dirs.
3. Don't change `tool-version-check.sh` behaviour unless step 1 shows a real product defect.

## Verification

- The test prints `PASS: Homebrew updates installed formulas and installs absent selected formulas` on a host with real `glab`/`rg`/`shellcheck`/`wt` installed, and still passes where those are absent.
- The other `test-tool-version-check-*.sh` tests still pass.

Found while verifying #36394 (PR #36395); that change touches only the npm category, and this test runs `--category brew`.

title: Cloudflare email-routing reference: warn that enabling a subdomain also adds an apex SPF record (can break existing Google/M365 mail)
body:
Observed 2026-11-01: POST /zones/{zone_id}/email/routing/dns with body {"name": "marketing.<domain>"} on a zone whose apex MX is Google Workspace correctly added MX + SPF on the subdomain only (as previewed by GET /email/routing/dns?subdomain=...), but ALSO silently created an apex TXT 'v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all' (where the apex had no SPF) and a locked apex DKIM record cf2024-1._domainkey. The apex SPF would make the existing provider's outbound mail fail SPF. Zone email routing status became 'misconfigured' (mx.foreign) but subdomain status was 'ready' and forwarding worked. Also: the dashboard offers only apex onboarding (which proposes replacing apex MX); subdomain enablement on a zone with a foreign apex MX is API-only. Required token permissions for the settings/dns endpoints: Zone Settings Write (+ Email Routing Rules Write, DNS Write, Account Email Routing Addresses Write); without Zone Settings the API returns code 10000. Destination verification links are behind a Cloudflare challenge and fail in headless browsers. Proposed fix: add these to .agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-skill/references/email-routing/gotchas.md (and configuration.md): subdomain enablement via API, snapshot DNS before/after, delete the apex SPF if the apex had none (or merge includes if it had one), keep the locked DKIM. Verify: docs mention apex SPF side effect, required permissions, and the before/after DNS diff step.

title: Cloudron release approval: recover from a failed request instead of stalling behind a bare hold
body:
## What

A Cloudron package release PR can stall forever when the worker's `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request <repo> <pr>` fails. Make a failed request recoverable without maintainer intervention, keeping the signed-approval boundary.

## Evidence

Package repo PR #56 (opendesk 0.2.10, worker on v3.39.103, 2026-10-31 09:18Z):

1. The worker's `request` failed with `GitHub REST core budget exhausted (remaining 0)` before it added any label or created the release issue.
2. To protect the PR, the worker then added a plain `hold-for-review` label by hand (timeline: `labeled hold-for-review` 09:23:36Z). The PR body says: "Pulse should retry the release-approval request after REST budget recovery."
3. Nothing retried it. About 34 hours later, a manual `request` run failed with `ERROR: Resolve existing PR hold/auto-merge before requesting a release.` The guard at `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:184` accepts a PR with `hold-for-review` only when `release-approval-required` is also present.
4. Interactive recovery: adding `release-approval-required`, which mirrors the helper's own step at line 186, then re-running `request` created the release issue correctly.

## Reproducer

On a Cloudron package PR that passes `request`'s preconditions:

```bash
gh pr edit <pr> --repo <owner/package-repo> --add-label hold-for-review   # what the worker did after its request failed
cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request <owner/package-repo> <pr>
# ERROR: Resolve existing PR hold/auto-merge before requesting a release.
cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply                     # observed: r924 ran every 30 min for ~34h without creating the missing release issue
```

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-packaging.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`

Integration scope recovery: the existing request tests assert exit code 1 for label API failures and the scope-only process fixture stubs held reconciliation but not the new retry path. Update this existing suite to verify exit code 4, failure recovery/idempotency, and the unchanged signature/bare-hold boundary. title: Worktree creation refusal follow-ups: verify enrollment on continuation, report base-dir failures
body:
## What

Two follow-ups from the CodeRabbit review of PR #36404 (GH#36370) that pre-date that PR and are outside its scope.

1. **Retained-worktree continuation skips enrollment verification.** When native worktree creation succeeds in Git but generation enrollment is refused, the tree is retained. `pre-edit-check.sh` loop mode then prints `CONTINUATION_COMMAND: worktree-helper.sh add <branch>`. That plain `add` accepts an existing worktree, so a caller can continue with the enrollment refusal still unresolved. - `.agents/scripts/worktree-paths.sh` — `aidevops_ensure_worktree_base_dir`.

title: fix(terminal-blocker): vacuous readiness probe releases fleet capability hold, redispatching runner_capability_unmet forever
body:
## What

Stop the fleet capability hold in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` from being released by a readiness probe that verified nothing. Today a `runner_capability_unmet` issue whose brief declares no checkable requirement is redispatched by every runner, about every 2 hours, without limit.

## Evidence (#36194)

- Between 2026-10-31 03:43Z and 2026-11-01 20:06Z, 14 dispatch attempts by two runners each ended with the same terminal blocker: `revision=c8c36f1b6553fe24d37d1cf3 blocker=0738181c7fb715c10ad8e589` (`runner_capability_unmet`). There were 9 observations from one login and 3 from another. Each attempt posted 4–6 ops comments and 6 label transitions, for 80 comments in total.
- A read-only replay of the production functions against the live comments showed:
  - `terminal_blocker_task_revision` = `c8c36f1b…`, matching every observation.
  - `_terminal_blocker_fleet_observations` returns 2 distinct runners on that revision, so the hold condition is met.
  - `_terminal_blocker_fleet_ready` returns success, so the hold is released.
- Why readiness passes:
  - `runner_capability_check` prints `requirements=0` and exits 0 when the brief declares no secrets, probes, SSH commands or `dispatch-class:` labels.
  - `worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh probe` reports `ready` (tsc present) or `not-applicable:*` for repos without JS dependencies.
  - Neither signal says anything about the prerequisite that actually failed. In #36194 that was runner-local data: the full repo registry and quarantined worktree ownership.
- Every new failure changes the per-runner checkpoint key, so the same vacuous probe "wakes" the hold again. `terminal_blocker_backoff_active` deliberately excludes `runner_capability_unmet` releases (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:939`), so nothing bounds the loop.

## Reproducer

Read-only, against live #36194 comments:

```bash
source .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
brief=$(gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/36194)
comments=$(terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments 36194 marcusquinn/aidevops "$(gh api user --jq .login)")
rev=$(terminal_blocker_task_revision "$brief" marcusquinn/aidevops 36194 "$PWD" runner_capability_unmet)   # c8c36f1b…
fp=$(_terminal_blocker_hash v2:runner_capability_unmet)                                                  # 0738181c…
_terminal_blocker_fleet_observations "$(_terminal_blocker_fleet_authorize "$comments" marcusquinn/aidevops)" "$rev" "$fp"  # 2 runners
_terminal_blocker_fleet_ready "$PWD" "$brief" && echo released   # prints "released" before the fix
```

## How

In `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`:

1. `_terminal_blocker_fleet_ready`: count readiness only when it is positive evidence. Either the brief declares at least one runner-checkable requirement and all of them pass (`runner_capability_check ... fresh` stderr `requirements=N`, N > 0), or the JS readiness probe/policy is `ready`/`current`. With `requirements=0` and `not-applicable:*` JS, the runner is not ready.
2. `terminal_blocker_fleet_hold_active`: once the hold has formed (2 distinct authenticated runners on the current revision), any later observation on the same revision means a probe-ready launch was falsified. From then on readiness can no longer release the hold. Only a brief revision (which changes the task revision) or an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` posted after the latest observation can release it. Emit `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_FLEET_HOLD ... probe=falsified wake=brief_or_retry`.
3. Keep the existing contract: no labels or issue comments are written by this gate, and other runners stay eligible until 2 distinct runners have observed the blocker.

Reference pattern: the retry handling in `terminal_blocker_runner_capability_observation_epoch` (`_terminal_blocker_latest_retry_comment` + `_terminal_blocker_retry_after`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A replay against #36194's comments returns a fleet hold (`probe=falsified`).
- [ ] An existing `test_fleet_capability_hold` case still passes: two observations plus a ready probe release the hold.
- [ ] A third observation after the hold formed keeps the hold even when readiness passes; an OWNER/MEMBER retry posted after it releases the hold; a changed brief releases it.
- [ ] `requirements=0` with a `not-applicable:*` JS probe is not ready.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean, and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh

## Not verified

The per-login 6-hour capability cooldown (`_dispatch_skip_for_capability_cooldown`) did not stop one login retrying at 2–5 hour intervals. That runner's logs are not available here. If it recurs after this fix, investigate separately with that runner's `pulse.log` (`runner_capability_unmet cooldown`).

title: bug(workflow-sync): stale NO-WORKFLOW hides remote @main callers and push failures are opaque
body:
## What

Two defects in the workflow sync pair surfaced while finishing the #36194 rollout:

1. **Stale `NO-WORKFLOW` hides a remote caller.** `check-workflows-helper.sh` classifies from the local canonical clone. When that clone is behind `origin/<default>` and the workflow was added upstream, the row is `NO-WORKFLOW` (only annotated `local evidence; main is N commit(s) behind origin/main`). `sync-workflows-helper.sh` `_list_actionable_repos` drops `NO-WORKFLOW` rows unless `--install-missing` is set (`.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` around lines 964–985), so `--pin-floating` never reaches the apply-time reclassification added by GH#27726 / PR #27736. The repo silently keeps an executable `@main` caller.
2. **Push failures are opaque.** `_sync_write_commit_push` runs the push with `2>/dev/null` (around line 1371) and reports only `git push failed`. In the observed case the real cause was `repo-verify-pre-push.sh` blocking because a fresh linked worktree had no `node_modules`. That is actionable, but it was invisible in the helper output and in any worker log.

## Evidence

- Two registered maintainer repos had a remote `loc-badge.yml` caller at `@main`, but local clones were 2 and 16 commits behind. `check-workflows-helper.sh --json --repo <slug> --workflow loc-badge` returned `"classification":"NO-WORKFLOW"`, `"freshness":"behind"`, and `sync-workflows-helper.sh --workflow loc-badge --pin-floating --repo <slug>` printed `no actionable repos/workflows`. After converging the mirror (or running from a linked worktree off `origin/main`, which `_resolve_row_checkout` prefers), the same command returned `PLANNED`, and the PRs merged.
- For a JS repo, `--apply` returned `{"outcome":"FAILED","detail":"git push failed"}` on two separate rollouts (two leftover `chore/workflow-sync-*` worktrees, no PR). A manual `git push` from the apply worktree showed `[repo-verify][BLOCK] lint could not start: JavaScript lint tooling or plugins are unavailable in this worktree` and `tsc: command not found`.

## Reproducer

Defect 1 (needs a registered repo whose canonical clone is behind origin and whose `.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml` with a `loc-badge-reusable.yml@main` caller exists only on origin):

**Symptom command**:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh --json --repo <slug> --workflow loc-badge
bash .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh --workflow loc-badge --pin-floating --repo <slug>
```

**Actual output**:

```text
{"slug":"<slug>","workflow":"loc-badge","classification":"NO-WORKFLOW","note":"local evidence; main is 16 commit(s) behind origin/main",...,"freshness":"behind"}
[sync-workflows-helper.sh] no actionable repos/workflows (all CURRENT or NO-WORKFLOW).
```

Defect 2 (needs a JS repo with a declared lint/typecheck command and no durable `js_dependency_policy`):

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh --apply --workflow loc-badge --pin-floating --repo <js-slug> --json
# → "outcome":"FAILED","detail":"git push failed"
git -C <apply-worktree> push -u origin chore/workflow-sync-<date>
# → [repo-verify][BLOCK] lint could not start ... / tsc: command not found
```

## How

In `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh`:

- When freshness is `behind` (or `diverged`) and the local result is `NO-WORKFLOW`, classify from the remote default branch instead (e.g. `git show <remote>/<default>:.github/workflows/<file>` after the existing remote refresh, or `gh api .../contents` as fallback). If remote evidence is unavailable, emit an `UNKNOWN`/stale classification rather than `NO-WORKFLOW`. Reference pattern: `_classify_row_with_freshness` and `_repo_freshness` (around lines 660–1025).

In `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh`:

- Capture push stderr to a bounded temp file and include a one-line reason in the TSV/JSON `detail`. Recognise `[repo-verify][BLOCK]` and emit `git push blocked by repo-verify: <first BLOCK line>` plus the existing resolution pointer (`worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh approve`). Never print credentials or remote URLs with tokens.
- On a push failure, return the apply worktree to a clean state, or report its path so a rerun does not leave orphan `chore/workflow-sync-*` worktrees.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A registry row whose local clone is behind and lacks the workflow, while origin has an `@main` caller, is `PLANNED` by `sync-workflows-helper.sh --workflow loc-badge --pin-floating --repo <slug>` without manual mirror sync.
- [ ] A behind row with unavailable remote evidence is not reported as `NO-WORKFLOW`.
- [ ] A repo-verify pre-push block appears in `--json` `detail` with the BLOCK reason.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean on both helpers; the existing workflow-sync tests pass (`rg -l "sync-workflows-helper|check-workflows-helper" .agents/scripts/tests`).

title: fix(worktrees): same-boot census is never empty on Linux login accounts (non-dumpable ssh-agent/gpg-agent/sd-pam count as uncertain)
body:
## Problem

The #36282 fix (PR #36313, shipped in v3.39.108) lets cleanup reclaim same-boot worktrees only when two path censuses report `references == 0` **and** `uncertain == 0` (`worktree_lifetime_quiescence.py:38`, `empty_census`). On real Linux runner accounts `uncertain` is never 0. Same-UID **non-dumpable** tasks (`ssh-agent`, `gpg-agent`, systemd's `(sd-pam)`, the `sshd` session process) make `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, `fd/` and `environ` unreadable even to their owner, so `inspect_path_references` raises `PermissionError` and `collect_path_references` counts it as uncertain (`worktree_process_census.py:82-83`). Every same-boot worktree is preserved, and long-uptime runners still reach `AIDEVOPS_MAX_WORKTREES` and stop dispatching.

## Evidence (Linux runner host, v3.39.109, 2026-11-01, uptime 34 days)

- One runner user: `cleanup_worktrees.log` (last 4,000 lines) shows 849 `job-end` entries with **0 removals** in total, 107 × `same-boot process census active or unavailable` and 36 × `confirmed idle window incomplete`. Pulse logs 183 × `Live worktree count 206 >= cap` and 269 × `cleanup-lock-busy`, with 1 worker launched in 7 rounds while `available=24, candidates=66`.
- Running the shipped `path_census()` as each runner user on a path nobody uses gives `status=available references=0` and `uncertain=30` / `uncertain=4`. Attribution by task `comm`:
  - user A: `ssh-agent` 27, `gpg-agent` 2, `(sd-pam)` 1 (all `PermissionError`)
  - user B: `gpg-agent` 2, `(sd-pam)` 1, `sshd` 1 (all `PermissionError`)
- Even with leftover `ssh-agent`s killed, `gpg-agent` and `(sd-pam)` remain on any normal login account, so the census can never be empty.

## Reproducer

Setup: Linux, a runner user with a login session (systemd user manager) or a running `gpg-agent`/`ssh-agent`.

**Symptom command:** `cd ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts && python3 -c 'import worktree_process_census as c; r=c.path_census("/nonexistent/x"); print(r["status"], r["references"], r["uncertain"])'`

**Actual output:**

```text
available 0 4
```

**Expected:** `uncertain` excludes same-UID tasks that provably cannot reference the path, so the result for an unreferenced path is `available 0 0`.

## Proposed fix

Classify an unreadable same-UID task as **not referencing** the path only when all of these hold. Otherwise keep it uncertain (fail closed).

1. `cwd`/`fd`/`environ` raise `PermissionError` (non-dumpable). Other errors stay uncertain.
2. Its start time (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22, still readable) is **earlier than the worktree's creation**. Use the registry's recorded creation/generation time, or the directory's birth time, so the task cannot have inherited the cwd or environment.
3. Its `comm` is in a small allowlist of daemons that `chdir("/")` and never open worktree paths: `ssh-agent`, `gpg-agent`, `(sd-pam)`, `systemd`, `sshd`, `dbus-daemon`.

Record the number of tasks classified this way in the census result (for example `excluded_nondumpable`) so receipts stay auditable. Keep `validate_quiescence` strict: samples must still have `uncertain == 0`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_census.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_quiescence.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-process-census.py`

## Verification

- New test: a non-dumpable allowlisted task started before the worktree yields `uncertain == 0`. The same task started after the worktree, or a non-allowlisted one, stays uncertain.
- On an affected runner, `cleanup_worktrees.log` shows `removed>0` for merged worktrees, and the Pulse worktree count drops below the cap without a reboot.

Follow-up to #36282.

title: fix: Cloudron release-approval supersede filter crashes on approval bodies
body:
## What

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request` never supersedes older unsigned release-approval issues. The jq filter that finds them errors out on every real approval body.

## Evidence

The `request` run for aidevops-cloudron-app PR 244 printed:

```text
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index array with string ("schema")
```

At `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:214`, the filter runs `map(fromjson? | select(.schema == 1))` over each body line. Every approval body has a `### Verification` line that is a JSON array of check results. `fromjson?` parses that line, then `.schema` on an array raises an error that `?` does not catch. The whole filter aborts with no output, so the supersede loop never runs. Minimal repro:

```bash
jq -nr '[{"number":1,"body":"{\"schema\":1,\"version\":\"0.1.41\"}\n[{\"bucket\":\"pass\"}]"}] | .[] | (.body | split("\n") | map(fromjson? | select(.schema == 1)) | .[0].version // "")'
```

## Fix

Use the same guard as `release_metadata` at line 222: `select(type == "object" and .schema == 1)`.

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:214`

## Verification

- The minimal repro, using the guarded filter, prints `0.1.41`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` passes.
- ShellCheck is clean.

title: bug(canonical-recovery): sync-mirror blocked forever by malformed .aidevops.json at stale HEAD
body:
## What

`canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror` cannot converge a canonical mirror whose **stale local HEAD** has a malformed `.aidevops.json`, even when that file has been fixed or removed on origin. Sync is the operation that would replace the stale HEAD, so the mirror stays behind until someone repairs it by hand.

## Evidence

From the #36194 rollout, on one registered maintainer repo:

- `git -C <canonical> status -sb` → `## main...origin/main [behind 16]`, with local edits to `.aidevops.json`, `.gitignore` and `TODO.md`.
- `git -C <canonical> show HEAD:.aidevops.json | jq .` → `parse error: Expected value before ',' at line 34, column 4`.
- `gh api repos/<slug>/contents/.aidevops.json` → `404` (the file no longer exists on the default branch).
- `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror --repo <canonical> --issue 36194 --confirm SYNCHRONIZE_CANONICAL_MIRROR` → `BLOCKED: configured branch metadata is unreadable: HEAD:.aidevops.json: Extra data: line 34 column 4 (char 790)`.
- After the remote merge, `full-loop-helper.sh merge` also reported `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true` for this repo, so every later merge leaves it stale.

## Reproducer

Setup: a disposable clone that is behind `origin/<default>`, whose HEAD commit has a malformed `.aidevops.json` (e.g. `{"default_branch":"main"},`), while origin's default branch has no `.aidevops.json`.

**Symptom command**:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror --repo <canonical> --issue <N> --confirm SYNCHRONIZE_CANONICAL_MIRROR
```

**Actual output**:

```text
BLOCKED: configured branch metadata is unreadable: HEAD:.aidevops.json: Extra data: line 34 column 4 (char 790)
```

**Expected**: the mirror converges to origin's default branch (dirty state preserved), because the remote default no longer carries the malformed file.

## How

In `.agents/scripts/canonical_branch_policy.py`, `_project_branch` (line 72) reads `HEAD:.aidevops.json` and raises on malformed JSON. `resolve_branch` (line 137) therefore aborts before trying `_origin_default_branch`.

- When `HEAD:.aidevops.json` is malformed, read the same file at the remote default ref (`<remote>/HEAD`, already resolvable via `_origin_default_branch`). If the remote copy is valid, use its branch (source `project-config-at-remote-default`). If the remote copy is absent, fall through to `_origin_default_branch`. If both are malformed, keep raising as today.
- Keep `registered-repo-config` as first precedence, and keep invalid branch names (`_valid_branch`) fatal.
- Callers to check for unchanged behaviour: `.agents/scripts/canonical-write-policy-helper.py`, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The reproducer converges: `SYNCHRONIZED_CANONICAL_MIRROR=true`, dirty state preserved by the existing backup path.
- [ ] A malformed config at both HEAD and the remote default still blocks with the current message.
- [ ] The existing canonical-branch-policy tests pass (`rg -l canonical_branch_policy .agents/scripts/tests`); `ruff`/`python3 -m py_compile` are clean if they are configured.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/canonical_branch_policy.py
- EDIT (if present): matching test under .agents/scripts/tests/

title: bug(js-readiness): approve records the approving shell's Node major, so the policy is stale in agent runtimes
body:
## What

`worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh approve` records `node_major` from whichever `node` is first on the approving shell's PATH (`_jsr_node_major`, `.agents/scripts/worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh:536`). When the owner's terminal and the agent runtime resolve different Node majors, a policy approved in the terminal is immediately `stale-node-major` everywhere it is consumed. The approval has no effect, and nothing at approval time says so.

## Evidence

From the #36194 rollout:

- The owner ran `worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh approve <repo>` in a terminal. The recorded policy was `{"package_manager":"npm","node_major":"24",...}`.
- In the OpenCode session (and therefore in its worktrees and pre-push), `status` returned `JS_DEPENDENCY_POLICY=stale-node-major` with `JS_DEPENDENCY_CURRENT={...,"node_major":"26"}`.
- The push stayed blocked until a separately approved one-off `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.

## Reproducer

Setup: approve from a shell whose `node` is major 24 (`PATH=<node24-bin>:$PATH ... approve <repo>`), then query from the agent runtime whose `node` is major 26.

**Symptom command**:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh status <repo-worktree>
```

**Actual output**:

```text
JS_DEPENDENCY_POLICY=stale-node-major
JS_DEPENDENCY_POLICY_RECORD={"approved_at":"2026-11-01T22:44:58Z","lockfile_sha256":"1e9e2d3c…","package_manager":"npm","node_major":"24","scope":"worktree-install"}
JS_DEPENDENCY_CURRENT={"package_manager":"npm","lockfile_sha256":"1e9e2d3c…","node_major":"26"}
```

**Expected**: the approval either applies to the runtime's Node, or `approve` warns at approval time that it will not.

## How

In `.agents/scripts/worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh`:

1. `approve`: print the resolved `node` path and major. If the major differs from the Node the aidevops runtime uses (detect via the same resolution the pulse/worker launch uses, or an `AIDEVOPS_NODE_BIN` override if one exists; otherwise state that it is unknown), warn explicitly and suggest `--node-major <N>`.
2. Accept `approve --node-major <N>` (repeatable). Store `node_majors` as a list; keep reading the legacy scalar `node_major`. Status/prepare match if the current major is in the list. Never widen the package manager, lockfile or scope checks.
3. Document the flag in `.agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md` ("Durable worktree install policy").

Reference pattern: the existing `--track-default-branch` option on `approve` (GH#35788) extends matching without loosening other checks.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Approving from Node 24 with `--node-major 24 --node-major 26` yields `JS_DEPENDENCY_POLICY=current` under Node 26.
- [ ] A legacy scalar `node_major` policy behaves as before.
- [ ] `approve` prints a mismatch warning when the runtime major is detectably different.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean; existing readiness tests pass (`rg -l worktree-js-readiness .agents/scripts/tests`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md
- EDIT (if present): matching test under .agents/scripts/tests/

title: fix(lifecycle): admission blocks every OpenCode tool when runtime owner pid is empty
body:
## What

Every OpenCode Bash, Edit/Write and `aidevops_bounded_operation start` call fails with
`BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable; no write authorized` on bundles built from
4ea0d654 onward (later 3.39.109 builds and 3.39.110), including fresh sessions and `pwd` in
non-repo directories. Separately, even on the working 8b25a674 bundle, `git -C ~/<path> ...`
is blocked with the same generic message.

## Why

The regression came in with #36403 (GH#36392):

1. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/runtime-owner.mjs` returns `pid=""` unless
   `sessionID === process.env.OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` and `OPENCODE_PID` /
   `OPENCODE_PID_START_IDENTITY` are set. Nothing sets those for the OpenCode server process
   (the `tool-install.sh` shim unsets them). Only `bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` passes
   `allowSelfFallback`.
2. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs` then passes `--runtime-pid ""` to
   `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py`. argparse (`type=int`) exits 2 before
   the `not-applicable` short-circuit for non-linked targets.
3. `lifecycle-admission.mjs` turns any non-JSON or unrecognised failure into the generic
   message, which hides the cause.
4. `worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py` `command_targets()` resolves `git -C ~/...` literally
   (no tilde expansion), raises `git-target-unavailable`, and reports only `ValueError`.
5. Plugin tests mask (1)-(2) because they set `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`/`OPENCODE_PID`/
   `OPENCODE_PID_START_IDENTITY` globally (`tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`).

## Reproducer

```bash
python3 -E -s -B .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py --cwd "$PWD" --runtime-pid "" --session-id x
# argparse: error: argument --runtime-pid: invalid int value: '' (exit 2)
```

In OpenCode on bundle 3.39.109-8b25a674, `pwd` passes but the Bash call
`git -C ~/<repo-path> status -sb` returns the generic BLOCKED message.

## How

- `worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py`: accept an empty/absent runtime pid. Non-linked targets
  (canonical or outside Git) return `not-applicable` without one; linked targets without a valid
  pid return `runtime-owner-unresolved`. Expand a leading `~` in `git -C` targets the way the
  shell would, and expose safe protocol reasons such as `git-target-unavailable`.
- `runtime-owner.mjs` / `lifecycle-admission.mjs`: when no inherited identity proof matches,
  fall back to the plugin process (`process.pid` + `processStartIdentity`), because the plugin
  runs inside the runtime that serves the session. Keep the inherited-proof path and the
  `#aidevops:trust-boundary` markers.
- `lifecycle-admission.mjs`: include the helper's safe reason and a recovery step in the BLOCKED
  message (no host paths or secrets).
- Check `.agents/hooks/git_safety_lifecycle.py` for the same empty-identity pattern.

## Verification

- `python3 -E -s -B .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py --cwd "$PWD" --runtime-pid "" --session-id x`
  returns JSON instead of exiting 2.
- Plugin tests: `test-git-safety-gate.mjs`, `test-bounded-worktree-ownership.mjs` and
  `test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs`, plus a case with the three env vars unset and a session ID
  that doesn't match `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`.
- After release and deploy, `pwd` and `git status` work in a new OpenCode tab and in a `/new` session.

title: Canonical Git guard blocks OpenCode undo snapshots (git add/gc on the private snapshot git-dir)
body:
## What

OpenCode's built-in undo snapshot runs `git add` and `git gc` against its own snapshot git-dir,
with the canonical checkout as the work tree. The canonical Git guard classifies that as canonical
mutation and blocks it every few seconds:

```text
failed to add snapshot files ... BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add' (exitCode=42)
```

## Reproducer

Open an OpenCode session whose project root is a registered canonical checkout, edit nothing,
and watch the OpenCode log: the error above repeats every few seconds.

## Why

- The OpenCode log floods with the same error every few seconds.
- Undo snapshots are disabled for sessions rooted in a canonical checkout.
- The snapshot repository is OpenCode-private storage (`--git-dir` under the OpenCode data
  directory's `snapshot/` tree), not the canonical repository's `.git`, so blocking it protects nothing.

## How

Option A (preferred): in `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py` (policy in
`.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`, invocation parsing in
`.agents/scripts/canonical_git_invocation.py`), exempt invocations whose explicit `--git-dir`
resolves inside the OpenCode data directory's `snapshot/` tree and is not the work tree's own Git
dir. Keep the exemption structural: require the resolved git-dir to sit under the runtime's
snapshot root, and mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

Option B: have the launcher or setup disable OpenCode snapshots for sessions rooted in a
registered canonical checkout (`"snapshot": false` in OpenCode config), so undo still works in
linked worktrees.

Reference pattern: earlier read-only exemptions such as `git check-ignore` (GH#33858).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: add a case where `git --git-dir <snapshot-root>/<id> --work-tree <canonical> add .`
  is allowed and the same command with the canonical `.git` as git-dir is still blocked.
- After deploy, open an OpenCode session in a canonical checkout and confirm the log no longer contains
  `failed to add snapshot files` with exitCode=42.

Low priority; not part of #36430.

title: tests/test-git-safety-guard.py is unwired and fails on main (import path, empty session id)
body:
## What

`tests/test-git-safety-guard.py` isn't wired into any runner, and it already fails on `main`.

## Reproducer

```bash
python3 tests/test-git-safety-guard.py
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'git_safety_lifecycle'
env PYTHONPATH=.agents/hooks python3 tests/test-git-safety-guard.py
# FAILED (failures=5) ... lifecycle owner admission unavailable (invalid-session-identity)
```

## Why

Found while verifying #36430. Two problems, both present before that PR:

1. Running `python3 tests/test-git-safety-guard.py` fails at import with
   `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'git_safety_lifecycle'`. The test loads
   `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py` by file path without adding `.agents/hooks` to `sys.path`.
2. With `PYTHONPATH=.agents/hooks`, 5 linked-worktree cases fail. The fixture passes an empty
   `session_id` to the hook, so lifecycle admission refuses linked targets with
   `invalid-session-identity`. (Since #36430 the denial shows the reason; before, the message was generic.)

No CI job or linter references the file (`rg test-git-safety-guard.py` finds nothing), so the drift went unnoticed.

## How

- `tests/test-git-safety-guard.py`: insert `HOOK_PATH.parent` into `sys.path` before `exec_module`,
  and give linked-worktree `_check` calls a non-empty session id plus an isolated

title: Tabby recovery relaunches OpenCode in a stale pre-migration parent directory
body:
## What

Tabby session recovery keeps relaunching OpenCode in a stale pre-migration directory.
After the `<workspace>/<owner>/<repo>` layout migration, many recovery markers
(`opencode-tabby-recovery/<session>/recovery.json` under the aidevops work directory) still record
the old `<workspace>/<owner>` directory. That path still exists, but now only as the
non-repository parent of the registered repository. A marker written after the migration still had it, so each
restore re-records the stale path.

Local survey (read-only, counts only): 115 markers point at a non-Git directory that contains
exactly one `repos.json`-registered repository. 179 point at ordinary non-repository directories
such as the user's home directory. Those are legitimate and must keep working.

## Reproducer

1. Create a private recovery marker directory `opencode-tabby-recovery/ses_xxxxxxxx/` whose
   `recovery.json` (schema 1) records `directory` = a non-repository directory `P` that contains
   one registered repository `P/<repo>`.
2. Run `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs resolve --cwd <marker dir> --work-dir <work dir>`.
3. Observed: stdout reports `P` as the launch directory, so OpenCode starts in the non-repository
   parent and the plugin re-records `P`. Expected: `P/<repo>`.

## Why

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh` `apply_tabby_recovery` prefers the marker
  directory over the invocation directory.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs` `resolveSessionRecoveryMarker`
  only checks that the path still exists (`realpathSync`).
- The relaunched session's plugin writes the same stale `directory` back on `session.updated`,
  so the loop never ends.
- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py` `recovery_marker_consumers` retargets only exact
  mapping matches present at migration time. Markers rewritten afterwards by still-running
  sessions are missed. Applied migration plans do not map these paths, so there is no
  authoritative old-to-new mapping to retarget through.

## How

In `resolveSessionRecoveryMarker`, classify the marker directory before using it:

- Inside a Git work tree: unchanged.
- Not inside a Git work tree, and `<dir>/<basename(dir)>` is a Git repository registered in
  `repos.json` (the exact shape the migration produced): relaunch in that repository. The resumed
  session then writes a corrected marker, which breaks the loop. Session-row validation accepts
  the row when both sides relocate to the same repository.
- Any other shape (home directory, the workspace root holding several personal repositories, an
  organisation directory with a differently named repository): unchanged, as today. A count-based
  remap/reject rule was considered and rejected: it would reject legitimate sessions opened in a
  directory holding several repositories and guess for differently named single children.
- `repos.json` comes from `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_JSON`, falling back to the default aidevops config
  location, as in `gpt-image-worktree.mjs`.

**Decision update (PR review):** implemented as the exact-shape rule above; all 115 affected local
markers have that shape.

Reference pattern: `canonicalMarkerDirectory` / `readRecoveryMarker` validation style in the same file.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-data.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-layout.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh` (only if a launcher-level case is needed)

## Verification

- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs`: cover a marker whose directory is
  the stale owner directory of a registered same-named repository (relocated), of an unregistered
  one (unchanged), and plain non-repository directories (unchanged).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh` passes.

title: OpenCode undo snapshots blocked by canonical Git guard in canonical checkouts (log flood, exit 42)
body:
## What

OpenCode's internal undo-snapshot feature runs `git --git-dir <opencode data>/snapshot/<project> --work-tree <checkout> add …` (and periodic `git gc`) against the session's project directory. When that directory is a canonical aidevops checkout, the canonical Git guard blocks it:

```
failed to add snapshot files … BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add' … exitCode=42
```

The log line repeats every few seconds in `opencode.log`, and undo snapshots are disabled for canonical sessions.

## Reproducer

1. Start OpenCode with its project directory set to a canonical (non-linked) checkout of a repository registered in repos.json.
2. Make any edit attempt or wait for the snapshot timer.
3. Observed: `opencode.log` records `failed to add snapshot files` with `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard` and exit code 42 every few seconds.
4. Expected: the snapshot repository (a separate Git dir owned by OpenCode's data home) is not treated as a canonical worktree mutation, or snapshots are disabled cleanly for canonical sessions without log spam.

**Symptom command:** `git --git-dir <opencode data>/snapshot/<project> --work-tree <canonical checkout> add .` (issued by OpenCode's snapshot module through the aidevops Git shim)

**Actual output:** `failed to add snapshot files … BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add'. Use a linked worktree for edits. …` with `exitCode=42`, repeated every few seconds in `opencode.log`.

## Why

The guard classifies by the effective repository identity (`--work-tree` resolves to the canonical top level), even though the object store and index written are in OpenCode's private snapshot Git dir, not the canonical repository's `.git`. The canonical checkout's refs, index and objects are never touched by these commands.

## How

Two options; pick one after verifying OpenCode's exact argv (capture one blocked invocation from the log):

- **A (preferred):** in `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` `_classify_canonical_operation` (or before `_is_canonical` in `classify_git_argv`), allow `add`, `write-tree`, `read-tree`, `gc`, `prune` and similar snapshot operations only when the prefix carries an explicit `--git-dir` whose real path is inside OpenCode's snapshot directory (`<data dir>/opencode/snapshot/`) and whose common dir differs from the canonical repository's common dir. Mark the check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Never allow when `--git-dir` resolves to the canonical `.git` or any linked worktree's git dir.
- **B:** disable OpenCode snapshots for canonical-checkout sessions via the launcher/config (`snapshot: false`) so no blocked commands are attempted.

Reference pattern: the existing narrow exceptions `_is_isolated_prospective_merge_tree` and `_is_isolated_routines_publisher` in the same file.

Files:
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` (exception), or the OpenCode launcher/config path for option B.
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/` canonical guard tests (search `rg -l canonical-git-command-guard .agents/scripts/tests`).

## Acceptance

- A snapshot `git --git-dir <snapshot dir> --work-tree <canonical> add .` is allowed; the same command with `--git-dir` pointing at the canonical `.git` (or a path outside the snapshot root) is still blocked.
- No `failed to add snapshot files … canonical Git guard` lines in `opencode.log` during a canonical session.
- Priority: low.

title: Bash gate: lifecycle owner admission OperationalError while two commit-and-pr operations run concurrently
body:
## Observed

In an interactive OpenCode session (aidevops v3.39.111, OpenCode v1.19.5, macOS), the Bash tool's command gate rejected ordinary commands with:

```text
BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable (OperationalError); no write authorized
```

It happened twice in one session, both times while two `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` operations ran at the same time through `aidevops_bounded_operation`, each in its own linked worktree of the same managed project repo. Blocked commands included read-only `git diff --stat <sha> HEAD -- <path>` and a local `pnpm exec turbo run build` inside a third linked worktree. In both cases the gate recovered without intervention once one of the two commit-and-pr operations finished. A merge (`full-loop-helper.sh merge`) running alongside a single commit-and-pr did not trigger it. Earlier in the same session the lifecycle store was inspected and found readable (schema 2), with worktrees intact.

## Expected

Concurrent commit-and-pr operations in separate worktrees should not make the admission store unavailable to other tool calls. Read-only commands should not need write admission at all.

## Likely area (unverified)

The lifecycle owner admission store is probably held under a lock or a long write transaction by the commit-and-pr validator or push phases (SQLite `OperationalError: database is locked`). Candidates: a busy timeout on the admission connection, shorter transactions in commit-and-pr, or classifying read-only commands before requiring admission.

## Workaround

Run commit-and-pr operations one at a time. Merges can run alongside a single commit-and-pr.

## Verification

Start two `commit-and-pr` operations in separate linked worktrees of one repo, then run `git status` in a third worktree while both are in their validator phase. It should succeed and never return `OperationalError`.

title: Bug: exact-value redaction masks a managed private repo slug, blocking supervisor recovery for that repo
body:
## What

In an unattended supervisor-pulse session (OpenCode, v3.39.108), exact-value credential redaction replaced **both the owner and the name of a managed private repository slug** with the redaction token in every tool output: the pre-fetched `pulse-state.txt`, `aidevops repos` (path basename), `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` JSON (repo field shown as token/token) and worker failure excerpts.

The display name in `aidevops repos` is still visible, so the redaction is not a privacy feature. It comes from `registered-value-sources.mjs` exact-value matching: some locally registered credential value of 8+ characters equals the owner and/or repo-name token.

## Impact (observed)

The supervisor cannot address that repo at all. Every slug-keyed read or write needs the literal slug, and the session cannot know it without decoding the redaction. Affected commands:

- `gh issue view N --repo SLUG`
- `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh record SLUG N`
- `recovery-policy-helper.sh SLUG`
- `pulse-wrapper.sh --command list-candidates SLUG`

The shared command policy also correctly blocks `xargs`-style indirection. In this sweep, 2 pending terminal-blocker entries for that repo could not be verified or recorded. 38 issues stranded by the lifecycle-admission defect could not be recovered (#36457). The repo's ~50 open PRs and ~75 open issues get no LLM triage. The deterministic wrapper is not affected.

## Expected

A value that is a public identifier for the operator is not redacted as a bare credential. Specifically, the `owner` and `name` components of `slug` values in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`, and repo path basenames, pass through. Assignments whose variable name looks sensitive (names ending in TOKEN, SECRET or PASSWORD) are still scrubbed.

## How (worker guidance)

- Pattern to extend: `IDENTIFIER_ENV_NAME` / `PUBLIC_VALUE_PATTERN` and `usableValue()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/registered-value-sources.mjs`. `PUBLIC_VALUE_PATTERN` was added for the same class of bug with the literal `aidevops` (closed #35829); `IDENTIFIER_ENV_NAME` handles names ending in USERNAME (closed #34566).
- Add a cached set of public identifiers read from `repos.json` slugs (`owner`, `name`, full `owner/name`), keyed on mtime/size like `fileSignature`. Exclude matching values in `usableValue()`.
- Mirror the exemption in `.agents/scripts/redaction-digest-registry.py`, the file the existing comments say must stay in sync.
- Do not log or echo the matched values.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/registered-value-sources.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/redaction-digest-registry.py`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs`

Extend the existing test cases rather than adding a new harness.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs` passes, with a new case: a registered credential value that equals a `repos.json` slug component passes through as a bare occurrence, but is still scrubbed when assigned to a sensitive-named variable.
- `python3 -m py_compile .agents/scripts/redaction-digest-registry.py`.
- On a host with this condition, `aidevops repos` shows the full path and the supervisor prompt's state file shows the slug.

Reproducer note: the exact credential name and value on the observing host are intentionally not recorded. Reproduce with a synthetic credentials-file export named FOO_DB_NAME with value `examplerepo`, and a `repos.json` slug `example-owner/examplerepo`.

title: Bug: lifecycle-admission tool refusals project reason=unknown status:blocked and strand issues after the fix
body:
## What

When the OpenCode plugin's own lifecycle-admission gate refuses every worker tool call, the worker exits with an unclassified `BLOCKED:` line. The runtime records `reason=unknown` and projects `status:blocked` (GH#35745 holds `unknown` as blocked). That hold re-arms only on a brief/dependency revision or an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`. So after the infrastructure defect is fixed, every victim issue stays blocked indefinitely.

## Evidence (one Linux runner, 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-02)

- 48 local worker-failure excerpts (`~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts/`) contain the tool error `"error": "BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable; no write authorized"`. It is thrown at `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs:108`. Read-only `gh issue view`, `git status` and `git log` were refused too.
- They cover 41 distinct issues between 2026-11-01T05:49Z and 2026-11-02T00:30Z: 3 here (#36336, #36421, #36422) and 38 in one managed private repo.
- The root causes were fixed by #36430 and #36448 (both COMPLETED by 2026-11-02T04:21Z). No refusals have occurred since 00:30Z, and workers on the same runner complete normally.
- Every victim's public release comment reads `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown ... Projected state: status:blocked.` `pulse-check-helper.sh json` reports `blocked_explicit_hold: 77` while 24 slots sit idle.
- The supervisor manually recovered #36422 and #36336 with recovery comments and `gh-write-helper.sh issue status ... available`. The private-repo victims could not be reached in-session (see #36456).

## Expected

A blocked exit caused by framework runtime gates refusing the worker's tools is runner-local infrastructure failure, not an issue blocker. It should stay `status:available` under the existing dispatch backoff, like `runner_capability_unmet` without missing secret names (`_hrff_blocked_exit_holds`). Issues already held this way should re-arm once the runner's runtime no longer reproduces the refusal.

## How (worker guidance)

1. **Classify deterministically**, not from model prose. Have the plugin record a structured admission-refusal event or counter per session, which `lifecycle-admission.mjs` already owns. At worker exit, `headless-runtime-failure.sh` / `headless-runtime-result.sh` maps "zero successful tool calls, ≥1 admission refusal" to the runner-local class. Reuse `runner_capability_unmet`, or add an infrastructure class that `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` excludes.
2. **Backfill existing holds** in `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (discover/rearm stage). For a queued or discovered `unknown` hold, if this runner's protected excerpt for that repo and issue has the admission-refusal tool error and the runtime has been refusal-free for a full pulse window, return the issue to `status:available` exactly once. This is the helper's one sanctioned issue write (GH#33138). It needs no retry directive or label edits beyond that.
3. Keep fail-closed: excerpts are matched by issue number, so confirm the repo. Never re-arm permission, secret or `files_scope_excluded` holds this way.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

Scope notes: the plugin change emits refusal evidence only, with no admission-policy change. In `headless-runtime-failure.sh`, change `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` and the release projection. `headless-runtime-result.sh` owns exit classification. The recovery helper gets the re-arm backfill. Extend the existing test cases rather than adding a new harness.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes, with cases where (a) an exit whose only tool results are admission refusals projects `status:available`, and (b) an `unknown` hold whose excerpt has the refusal signature re-arms exactly once and not again.
- `shellcheck` on the touched scripts; `node --test` for any touched plugin test.
- Live: after deployment, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh rearm` on the affected runner returns its remaining admission-refusal victims to `status:available`.

title: fix: retain terminal accounting for unexpected worker exits
body:
## Goal

Record unexpected worker EXIT-trap termination as an explicit incomplete task and retain its canonical runtime metric, without treating process status zero as proof of completion.

Implementation is already owned by this interactive session in PR #36462. This issue is assigned and in review; do not start a parallel implementation.

## Reproducer

On candidate commit `5f234557f6a92e42aaf087dba59d6d6bc5a34b41`, run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh`. The added `clean/trap` case drives the real EXIT handler with a deterministic `clean` classification and process status zero, using disposable receipt/metric paths and stubbed preservation/release operations. It requires one failed metric with `worker_incomplete_exit`, raw exit status zero and an external receipt with the same reason. Other cases check normal-metric deduplication and subsequent-run accounting.

The original read-only observation was a terminal receipt with `reason=clean`, status zero and the last recorded lifecycle stage still `waiting_for_worker`, while the transcript lacked a completion/blocker handoff and the canonical metrics file had no matching attempt. In the parent source, the EXIT-trap finalizer lacks a canonical metric call and preserves the unqualified `clean` reason. Do not replay a live attempt to reproduce this accounting defect; the fixture exercises the relevant terminal path without live effects.

## Evidence

The EXIT-trap fallback can classify a zero-status wrapper termination with model activity as `clean`, even when normal result handling never finished. The finalizer writes external receipts and other terminal evidence but does not call the canonical metric writer, so runtime summaries can omit the attempt. The interruption trigger remains unknown; do not infer a signal, timeout or provider failure from the accounting gap.

## Implementation scope and references

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`: extend `_hrff_finalize_exit_trap` after existing preservation/checkpoint recovery. Keep typed completion and deferred checkpoints distinct, emit a missing canonical metric and use `worker_incomplete_exit` for otherwise unqualified `clean` termination.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`: reuse `append_runtime_metric`; acknowledge successful writes per invocation so an EXIT trap does not duplicate normal accounting or suppress the next run.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh`: extend the existing disposable-path suite using the real receipt and metric writer, with preservation/release operations stubbed.

Do not deploy, restart services, retry paused workers, bypass ownership/pause guards, delete locks or retire worktrees. Preserve raw process status and continue terminal handoff if metric persistence fails.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh`

- Bash syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

The candidate passes required changed-file lint and 183 targeted assertions. PR #36462 documents the wider runtime-suite missing-log failure reproduced on clean upstream and a pre-existing stale runtime-events structural assertion.
